subject: Historia
title: The Cold War
sourceSummary: The conflict between the USA and the Soviet Union after the Second World War — the Iron Curtain, the Berlin Wall, the arms race, and how it all eventually ended without a direct war between the superpowers.
topics: the Iron Curtain and the Berlin Wall
the end of the Cold War

questions.prompt: What did the Cold War involve?
questions.opener: The name "cold" war says something about what did NOT happen directly between the superpowers.
choices: A prolonged political and ideological conflict between the USA and the Soviet Union, without the countries fighting each other directly
An armed war in which American and Soviet troops met on the battlefield
A war between Germany and France in the 1980s
An economic union between Eastern and Western European countries
questions.explanation: The Cold War (c. 1947–1991) was a prolonged tension between the USA and the Soviet Union, marked by ideological rivalry between capitalism and communism, an arms race, and a power struggle for influence around the world — but without a direct war between the two superpowers themselves.

questions.topic: the Iron Curtain and the Berlin Wall
questions.prompt: What was meant by the "Iron Curtain"?
questions.opener: It is not a physical curtain, but an image for a political and military border.
choices: The political and military border that divided Europe into a communist east and a capitalist west
A physical wall built around the whole of Europe
A trade agreement between the USA and the Soviet Union
The Soviet Union's nickname for Moscow
questions.explanation: The "Iron Curtain" was a symbolic term (coined by, among others, Winston Churchill) for the sharp political and military border that divided Europe between the Soviet-controlled communist states in the east and the Western democracies in the west during the Cold War.

questions.topic: the Iron Curtain and the Berlin Wall
questions.prompt: Why did East Germany build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
questions.opener: Think about what many East Germans were doing before the wall was built, and what the East German regime wanted to stop.
choices: To prevent residents of East Germany from fleeing to West Berlin and West Germany
To protect West Berlin from a Soviet invasion
To increase trade between east and west
To celebrate the end of the Second World War
questions.explanation: Large numbers of East Germans were fleeing to the freer and wealthier West Berlin. To stop the exodus and maintain control, the East German regime built the Berlin Wall in 1961, which physically divided the city until 1989.

questions.prompt: What did the arms race between the USA and the Soviet Union during the Cold War involve?
questions.opener: Think about what "balance of terror" means — neither side dared attack because the opponent could strike back just as hard.
choices: The countries competed to build more and more powerful nuclear weapons, creating a balance of terror that deterred direct war
The countries competed over who could reduce their military the fastest
The arms race was purely about sporting competitions between east and west
The arms race ended before the Cold War had even begun
questions.explanation: Both the USA and the Soviet Union built up enormous arsenals of nuclear weapons. The idea was that if both sides could annihilate each other in an attack ("mutually assured destruction"), neither would dare strike first — an uneasy balance that kept the Cold War "cold".

questions.prompt: What was the Space Race an expression of?
questions.opener: Think about Sputnik and the Moon landing — what did the countries want to show the rest of the world?
choices: A technological and ideological prestige contest between the USA and the Soviet Union over who led in space technology
A scientific collaboration project between NASA and Soviet researchers
A competition over who could build the most bridges in Europe
A peace treaty that ended the Cold War
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union's launch of the satellite Sputnik in 1957 and the USA's Moon landing in 1969 were highlights of a Space Race in which both superpowers wanted to demonstrate technological and ideological superiority to the rest of the world.

questions.topic: the end of the Cold War
questions.prompt: Which event in 1989 became a powerful symbol of the end of the Cold War?
questions.opener: Think about the wall that had divided a city for decades.
choices: The Berlin Wall fell
The Soviet Union launched the satellite Sputnik
The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred
The Korean War began
questions.explanation: The fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 became a worldwide symbol that the Iron Curtain and the Cold War's division of Europe were dissolving. The Soviet Union was formally dissolved in 1991.

questions.topic: the end of the Cold War
questions.prompt: Explain why the Cold War ended and the Soviet Union was dissolved in 1991.
questions.opener: Think about the Soviet Union's economy, a new leader's reforms, and what happened in the Eastern Bloc in the late 1980s.
questions.answer: The Cold War ended through a combination of the Soviet Union's economic weakness, political reforms and popular movements in the Eastern Bloc. Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev introduced the reforms glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) to save a faltering economy, but they also opened the door to criticism and demands for change. When the Soviet Union no longer intervened militarily to support the Eastern Bloc's regimes, the communist governments fell quickly, symbolised by the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. The Soviet Union was finally dissolved in 1991 when its constituent republics declared independence.
steps: In the 1980s, the Soviet Union's economy was in deep crisis, with shortages of goods and an inefficient planned economy.
Gorbachev introduced glasnost (openness) and perestroika (economic reforms) to modernise the system.
The reforms created room for criticism of the regime and demands for more freedom, both in the Soviet Union and in the Eastern Bloc.
The Soviet Union refrained from intervening militarily when countries in the Eastern Bloc, such as East Germany, began reforming or rebelling.
The Berlin Wall fell in 1989, and in 1991 the Soviet Union was dissolved when the constituent republics declared independence.

questions.prompt: Summarise the Cold War's key features from beginning to end.
questions.opener: Think parties, border, arms race and how it all ended.
questions.answer: The Cold War (c. 1947–1991) was a political and ideological conflict between the USA (capitalism/democracy) and the Soviet Union (communism), without direct war between the superpowers · Europe was divided by the "Iron Curtain" between a communist east and a capitalist west · the Berlin Wall was built in 1961 to stop the exodus from East Germany and became a powerful symbol of the division · the arms race meant both sides built enormous arsenals of nuclear weapons, creating a "balance of terror" · the Space Race (Sputnik in 1957, the Moon landing in 1969) was part of the ideological prestige contest · Soviet leader Gorbachev's reforms glasnost and perestroika opened the door to change in the 1980s · the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 became a symbol of the end of the Cold War · the Soviet Union was dissolved in 1991, bringing the Cold War to an end.
